title: Finite locally free sheaves have finite free stalk modules.
statement: For a scheme X [def-pc-scheme], a finite locally free module sheaf M [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf] and x ∈ X, its stalk computed by [def-pc-module-stalk-functor] is both a free and a finite module over O_{X,x}.

source.place: Definition 17.14.1(2), taking stalks of the finite local frame

proof.text: Choose finite local generators data for M with an isomorphic presentation on every covering open. Choose a covering open U containing x and its finite index type I. Apply the already proved localStalkEquiv from Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteLocallyFreeStalkFinrank to this trivialization, obtaining M_x linearly equivalent to (I → O_{X,x}). This construction is accessed by a proof-only import all; it works for any finite I and requires no globally constant rank. Transfer Module.Free along the inverse equivalence and Module.Finite along its surjective underlying linear map. The empty index type gives the zero module, and the empty scheme has no point to check.

proof_origin.place: Definition 17.14.1(2), finite local frame; D4 repair reuses the proved localStalkEquiv construction through import all, rather than duplicating coordinate lemmas

lean.statement:
theorem stalk_isFiniteFree_of_isFiniteLocallyFree
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (M : X.Modules) [M.IsFiniteLocallyFree] (x : X) :
    Module.Free (X.presheaf.stalk x)
        ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace x).obj M) ∧
      Module.Finite (X.presheaf.stalk x)
        ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace x).obj M)
